candidates.title: walking-skeleton-claude-p
candidates.description: Walking skeleton: a run_agent(persona, inputs, schema) call that invokes claude -p headlessly as a subprocess, coerces the agent's output to a target JSON schema through a bounded validate->repair loop, and persists the resulting artifact into a vault via the vendored deterministic spine (vault_edit). One backend, one stage; no design tournament, Critic, or agentic tool-loop yet.
candidates.rationale: Exercises the riskiest dependency (the backend/model) and produces a touchable artifact (a schema-valid JSON file in a vault). Retires R-3 (structured-output + repair layer) and de-risks R-2 (first backend-adapter contract) and R-1 (strong-model path). Keeps the first cut under ~20% of scope per the no-full-parity-up-front non-goal (R-7). The run_agent signature is deliberately role/stage-aware from the start so per-stage backend routing (the near-term follow-on cut, ADR-003) plugs in without reworking the seam.

assumptions.statement: A Python adapter can invoke claude -p headlessly as a subprocess and capture its completion deterministically enough (persona as system prompt, inputs injected, model / output-format / flags controllable).
assumptions.spike_evidence: claude -p v2.1.206 invoked headlessly, rc=0, valid json envelope, no stderr
assumptions.fallback: Fall back to the Claude API (Anthropic SDK) as backend #1 if the CLI contract proves too unstable.
spike_constraints: invoke with --permission-mode dontAsk (not --dangerously-skip-permissions)
pass stdin=DEVNULL explicitly, never inherit
enforce a hard wall-clock timeout with process kill
pin a full model id for reproducibility
verify the Windows/PowerShell subprocess path

assumptions.statement: The claude -p output can be coerced to a target JSON schema through a bounded validate->repair loop reliably enough to write a valid artifact within a small retry budget.
assumptions.spike_evidence: first-try valid JSON, 0 repairs used; repair path not yet stress-tested
assumptions.fallback: Constrain output via --output-format json and/or a stricter repair prompt; cap retries and surface a hard failure.
spike_constraints: unwrap the --output-format json envelope (validate result/structured_output, not raw stdout)
keep validate->repair loop as source of truth; --json-schema is a hint only
add a truncation-detection branch for large payloads (~8-10k chars)

assumptions.statement: The vendored vault write path (vault_edit shim) runs correctly outside the Claude Code harness to persist the artifact.
assumptions.spike_evidence: vendored vault_edit wrote + read back an artifact to a scratch vault via AI_SDLC_VAULT_ROOT
assumptions.fallback: Thin reimplementation of the minimal write path if the vendored shim proves leaky.

candidates.verification_plan: From Python, invoke claude -p with a real persona + target schema; a schema-valid artifact lands in a scratch vault via the vendored vault_edit; a deliberately malformed first output is repaired within the retry budget; a hard failure surfaces cleanly when the budget is exhausted.

candidates.title: second-backend-claude-api
candidates.description: Add a 2nd backend adapter (Claude Messages API / Anthropic SDK) behind the SAME run_agent seam, letting the BackendAdapter interface EMERGE from two concrete implementations (ADR-002 / R-7) instead of being guessed from one. The API backend exposes an explicit max_tokens, so it can force a real max-output truncation and CONFIRM the M-add-1 truncation-signal branch (R-10 / code-review CR2) that claude -p v2.1.207 could not.
candidates.rationale: De-risks R-2 (the backend seam over 5 heterogeneous runtimes -- the highest-scored risk) by defining the interface against a 2nd concrete backend per ADR-002; retires R-10 by confirming the truncation early-abort empirically; keeps the pluggable-backend architecture honest before adding breadth (R-7).

assumptions.statement: The Claude Messages API (Anthropic SDK) drives run_agent behind the same seam and returns a completion coercible to the target schema, with an explicit max_tokens usable to force a real truncation.
assumptions.spike_evidence: GO on real account: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001; prompted-JSON validates + max_tokens=16 -> stop_reason=='max_tokens'. reality_proxy=real-account.
assumptions.fallback: Reuse the claude -p adapter contract; if the SDK response shape differs materially, adjust the emerging BackendAdapter interface rather than forcing the API into the CLI envelope shape.

candidates.verification_plan: Invoke run_agent through the Claude API backend against a real key; a schema-valid artifact persists + reads back; a small max_tokens forces a real truncation and the M-add-1 branch fires (TruncatedOutput) from the OBSERVED envelope signal.

candidates.title: secure-api-key-storage
candidates.description: Secure interactive API-key entry + encrypted storage for api-key backends. Prompt with getpass (no echo) and store/retrieve the key ENCRYPTED via the OS credential manager (keyring: Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service), plugging a keyring provider into the resolve_api_key() precedence chain built in slice-002 WITHOUT touching run_agent or the adapter. Replaces the plaintext .env dev-only fallback as the product mechanism.
candidates.rationale: The owner explicitly requested secure prompting + encrypted storage; slice-002 (ADR-005) shipped the resolve_api_key seam and deferred the keyring provider here to keep the backend-seam slice shippable. Additive behind the existing seam -- cheap reversibility.

assumptions.statement: keyring reads/writes the OS credential manager on the target platform(s) well enough for the app's setup flow (Windows Credential Manager confirmed first; macOS/Linux best-effort).
assumptions.spike_evidence: keyring 25.7.0 WinVaultKeyring; round-trip GO (set/get/delete, missing-key get None); rotation CONDITIONAL: get returns latest but a duplicate CredMgr entry appeared on re-set (keyring 545) -> design must delete-before-set. reality_proxy real-device.
assumptions.fallback: Encrypted file with a user passphrase (cryptography.Fernet), or continue env/config sourcing via the existing resolve_api_key seam.
spike_constraints: delete-before-set on rotation: delete_password before set_password so re-run/rotation never leaves a stale duplicate secret in the OS vault (keyring issue 545, reproduced on this Windows build).

runtime backend-class assertion before writing: require a known-secure OS credential backend (WinVaultKeyring on Windows), never fail.Keyring or a keyrings.alt plaintext backend; aivlc must never depend on keyrings.alt.
pass a stable non-empty account/username to all keyring calls (empty username is deprecated in keyring 25.x).
test AC5 keyring-unavailable fallback against a genuine NoKeyringError / fail.Keyring condition, not assumed.

candidates.verification_plan: getpass captures a key without terminal echo; keyring.set_password/get_password round-trips on the dev platform; resolve_api_key prefers keyring then falls back to env/config; the key never appears in any log sink.

candidates.title: harden-run-agent-robustness
candidates.description: Two advisory code-review hardenings from slice-001. CR3: tighten structured_output.parse_json so a first-balanced-object extraction from a MALFORMED outer wrapper (a complete nested object inside an unterminated wrapper) is rejected as ambiguous and fed to the repair loop, not persisted as a semantically-wrong-but-schema-valid artifact. CR5: wrap Popen's OSError (e.g. WinError 193 launching a .ps1 set as claude_bin) in a typed BackendInvocationError and exercise a synthetic .cmd/.ps1 shim launch, closing the m2 shim-launch claim.
candidates.rationale: Closes the two narrow correctness/robustness gaps code-review flagged on slice-001 (both minor, neither breaks an AC). Keeps the typed-error model TOTAL (every backend-launch failure -> typed) and AC4's 'no silent bad write' airtight against the nested-fragment edge.

assumptions.statement: parse_json can require the decode to consume to end (reject trailing non-whitespace / nested-only extraction) without breaking the m4 adversarial framings already covered.
assumptions.spike_evidence: The 5 m4 adversarial framings all place the object at top level after fence-strip, so requiring a full-consume keeps them green.
assumptions.fallback: Restrict the balanced-object scan to offset 0 after fence-stripping.

candidates.verification_plan: Adversarial parse test: a malformed outer wrapper with a valid nested object -> ambiguous -> repair loop (not persisted). Shim launch: a synthetic claude.cmd + claude.ps1 through cp._run_claude -> argv intact; a .ps1 that cannot exec -> typed BackendInvocationError (not raw OSError).

history.reason: no unproven blocking assumptions (A1 is non-blocking and already proven via slice-001-tests)

candidates.title: safe-cmd-argv-escaping
candidates.description: Replace slice-004/ADR-009's fail-closed .cmd/.bat metacharacter guard with a real fix: per-argument escaping (or a cmd.exe-safe launch wrapper / resolve-to-real-.exe launch that bypasses cmd re-tokenization) so a metacharacter-bearing prompt runs BYTE-INTACT in production when `claude` resolves to claude.cmd (the default npm Windows install), instead of being rejected. Addresses R-11 (command injection / BatBadBut / CVE-2024-24576).
candidates.rationale: The in-slice guard neutralizes the RCE but fails CLOSED -- legitimate prompts carrying & | < > ^ etc. on the .cmd path are refused. This restores full prompt fidelity safely (escape rather than reject) and may narrow ADR-009's deliberately-broad metachar set once real escaping exists. Scoped OUT of slice-004 (a minimal hardening slice) by TRI-1.

assumptions.statement: A reliable cmd.exe-safe escaping (or a direct-exec / resolved-.exe launch bypassing cmd re-tokenization) exists for .cmd/.bat argv on Windows, preserving arbitrary metacharacter-bearing prompts byte-intact without reintroducing injection.
assumptions.spike_evidence: resolve-past-shim direct-exec: 12/12 byte-intact (incl. newline + JSON), 0 injection; naive .cmd: 5/12 byte-intact. cmd.exe escaping ruled out (newlines unconditionally unescapable). Corroborated by field-recon (Rust/Node/BatBadBut). reality: local-real-data.
assumptions.fallback: Resolve claude to its real .exe (skip the .cmd shim) at config time, or keep the fail-closed guard and document the limitation.
spike_constraints: The safe launch MUST bypass cmd.exe: resolve the .cmd/.bat launcher to its underlying NATIVE executable and launch that directly via subprocess.Popen with a list argv (NO shell=True). Empirical: naive .cmd launch preserved only 5/12 metacharacter prompts byte-intact (& | < > ^ and any newline are mangled by cmd.exe); resolve-past-shim direct-exec preserved 12/12 (incl. newline + multi-line JSON) with 0/4 injections. Escaping is authoritatively dead (Rust CVE-2024-24576 returns InvalidInput; Node core: 'sometimes impossible to escape'); newlines are UNCONDITIONALLY unescapable through cmd.exe, and aivlc's argv[2] is always multi-line JSON.

Resolve the native target via the package install layout / package.json `bin` (e.g. node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/cli.js under the npm global prefix) or a robust resolver -- NOT by regex-parsing the .cmd shim TEXT (npm cmd-shim format has drifted across versions; shim-text parsing is fragile).

Prefer a native claude.exe when present (the 2026 native-installer default -- and the case on the current dev box) and only fall through to the shim-bypass for a genuine .cmd/.bat (legacy npm compat). Do NOT trust a single shutil.which('claude') to prefer .exe over .cmd -- enumerate candidates explicitly (Python 3.12 PATHEXT/which churn, cpython gh-127001).

If no launchable native target can be resolved, the launch MUST fail CLOSED with a typed BackendInvocationError (returncode=None) -- NEVER fall back to launching the .cmd/.bat directly (its injection-safety in the probe was incidental to Python quoting args-with-spaces, not robust).

candidates.verification_plan: On Windows with claude installed as claude.cmd: a prompt containing each of & | < > ^ " % ( ) ! launches successfully AND arrives at the child byte-intact (echo-shim round-trip), with NO injected command executed (marker-file negative check, as in slice-004's M3 test). The fail-closed guard is removed/narrowed only after this passes.

candidates.title: credential-lifecycle-ux
candidates.description: Add credential rotation / deletion / list UX on top of the slice-003 keyring store: an in-product way to clear or replace a stale/wrong stored key (m8: a present-but-wrong key silently shadows env and only surfaces as a later 401), plus first-class macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService verification (slice-003 shipped Windows-confirmed + best-effort; the ChainerBackend discovery shows real backends can chain, so the chainer-aware allowlist needs cross-platform reality contact).
candidates.rationale: Retires the stale-key trap m8 left only partially recoverable (store-success/miss hints), and turns the best-effort cross-platform keyring support into a proven path. Extends the ADR-007 credential store without touching run_agent or the adapter.

assumptions.statement: keyring delete_password + a stable-tag list/enumerate give a reliable rotate/clear on WinVault; macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService round-trip like Windows.
assumptions.spike_evidence: CONDITIONAL: core clear/rotate/delete->get-None all PASS on real WinVault (keyring 25.7.0); get_credential #698 NOT reproduced on 25.7.0; no value-free presence API (presence via get_password is-not-None); second-delete raises PasswordDeleteError (catch for idempotent clear); chainer fan-out + cross-platform unverified (leaf backend on this box) -- see spike-credential-lifecycle.
assumptions.fallback: Windows-only rotate/clear now; macOS/Linux remain best-effort until a real-device spike.
spike_constraints: clear MUST catch keyring.errors.PasswordDeleteError: on WinVault, delete_password on an already-absent entry RAISES (not a silent no-op), so idempotent clear requires the explicit catch (mirrors slice-003 set's swallow-not-found C1).

list/status has NO value-free presence API: presence must be derived from `get_password(account) is not None`; the plaintext transits process memory, so 'never exposes the secret' is a UI/print/log-layer guarantee only (never print/log the returned value) -- state this honestly, do not imply the secret is never decrypted.

Use get_password, NOT get_credential, for the presence check: #698 (get_credential returning another account's credential for a non-existent username) did NOT reproduce on the pinned keyring 25.7.0 (empirically verified here), but get_password is the narrower surface (returns only the string) and avoids the whole Credential-object false-positive class -- prefer it.

list is status-of-known-names, NOT a portable vault enumeration: keyring exposes no cross-platform 'list all accounts for a service' call, so list must iterate aivlc's own known/config-driven set of api-key env-var names and query per name; name it as such.

ChainerBackend delete/set fan-out is UNVERIFIED: this spike's box returned a LEAF WinVaultKeyring, so the multi-member-chain case (slice-003 saw a ChainerBackend led by WinVaultKeyring on a real box) could NOT be reality-tested here. delete_password may clear only the top-priority backend while a stale copy survives in a lower member -- design must not assume a single delete clears every chained member; flag for /critique and a future real-chained-box spike.

Cross-platform NOT reality-tested: macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService were NOT exercised (Windows-only proof, per the slice's scope decision). Keep the allowlist-guarded best-effort degrade for non-Windows backends; do NOT claim cross-platform clear/list proven -- that is deferred to its own candidate.

candidates.verification_plan: On each dev platform: store -> rotate (store again) -> get returns the NEW value with no duplicate (extends slice-003 #545 proof); delete -> get returns None -> resolve falls to env; a stale-key scenario is clearable in-product.

candidates.title: verify-cmd-launch-real-npm-install
candidates.description: Add a CI (or /validate-slice on a box with a real npm install) @real_claude .cmd smoke that npm-installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code and confirms slice-005's resolve-past-the-shim launch works against the REAL packaging: the native binary is delivered via a per-platform optionalDependency (@anthropic-ai/claude-code-win32-x64/claude.exe) linked by a postinstall SYMLINK into the sibling package. Closes AC1's deferred real-install residual + covers the bin-absent (--ignore-scripts / bun oven-sh#29399 / failed-postinstall) fail-closed edge that a synthesized fixture cannot surface.
candidates.rationale: slice-005 verified the SIMPLIFY resolver only against a SYNTHESIZED real-schema layout (reality_proxy=simulator) -- the dev box has the native-installer claude.exe, no npm .cmd install, so the real symlink/postinstall packaging was never contacted. Shrinking-legacy (npm install deprecated Jan 2026) but the only real-install proof of AC1.
spike_constraints: AC1 must assert only a present native .exe reached via package.json bin (is_file + --version rc=0); the real Windows postinstall writes bin/claude.exe as a real file in the main package (is_symlink=false, resolve==literal), so do NOT assert a symlink or a -win32-x64-sibling path.

AC3 must assert the DOWNSTREAM fail-closed guarantee at invoke_claude_p for both --ignore-scripts and --omit=optional real installs (no injection marker + typed BackendInvocationError via _run_claude CR5 or invoke_claude_p rc/envelope); do NOT assert _npm_shim_native_target returns None or that _run_claude raises -- the main package always ships a present bin/claude.exe placeholder.

The _npm_shim_native_target->None branch (legacy bin=cli.js / broken package.json) is NOT reachable via a real @anthropic-ai/claude-code install; cover it only with a synthesized layout (slice-005, simulator-grade), out of the real-install @real_claude smoke scope.

candidates.title: verify-credential-lifecycle-real-macos-linux-and-chained-backends
candidates.description: Reality-test the slice-006 credential lifecycle (delete/status/clear + resolve-falls-to-env) on the two real backend topologies NOT reachable on this Windows leaf-WinVault box: (a) macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService LIVE delete/status/clear round-trip (slice-006 shipped Windows-confirmed + allowlist-guarded best-effort on non-Windows), and (b) a REAL multi-member ChainerBackend -- does a single delete_password leave a stale copy in a lower member (keyring 25.7.0 delete is top-only per PR #740 while get_password reads all members)? Confirm delete-and-verify DETECTS the survivor and raises (ADR-013), and adjudicate the deferred bounded cross-member drain vs the current refuse+name-the-manual-step.
candidates.rationale: slice-006 defends the chained-survivor case UNCONDITIONALLY (detect-and-raise, value-free, names the manual OS-manager step) and keeps non-Windows best-effort, but neither the real chain nor macOS/Linux was reality-testable on this leaf-WinVault box (spike-credential-lifecycle constraints 5+6; ADR-013 residual). Closes the two remaining reality-contact gaps and adjudicates the bounded-drain deferral with real evidence.

assumptions.statement: macOS Keychain / Linux SecretService delete/status/clear round-trip like WinVault (delete->get None, idempotent-absent no-crash, value-free status).
assumptions.fallback: keep the allowlist-guarded best-effort degrade for non-Windows; do not claim cross-platform proven.

assumptions.statement: On a REAL multi-member ChainerBackend a single delete_password is top-only (PR #740) so a lower-member copy survives and get_password still returns it -- delete-and-verify detects it and raises CredentialStoreError.
assumptions.fallback: if delete does not fan out, add the deferred bounded cross-member drain (ADR-013) or keep refuse+name-the-manual-step.

candidates.verification_plan: On a mac + a linux box: store -> clear -> get None -> resolve falls to env; status value-free. On a box exhibiting a real ChainerBackend (slice-003 saw a WinVault-led chain): seed a lower-member copy, delete, confirm delete-and-verify raises (or, if delete fans out, that get->None).

history.reason: no blocking assumptions -- A1/A2 are non-blocking with fallbacks; reality-tested in-loop (AC1 local chain, AC2 CI Keychain/SecretService)

candidates.title: real-prove-invoke_claude_p-rc-envelope-fail-closed
candidates.name: real-prove the invoke_claude_p rc/non-JSON-envelope fail-closed guard against a REAL launchable-erroring not-delivered install
candidates.rationale: slice-007 real-proved the CR5 (WinError-216, returncode=None) not-delivered fail-closed edge via a real --ignore-scripts install, but the OTHER downstream guard -- invoke_claude_p's rc!=0 / non-JSON-envelope check -- was NOT reachable via a real not-delivered install on npm 11.12.0 (where --omit=optional delivers a FUNCTIONAL binary). It stays hermetic (slice-005 synthesized) + M1 build-verified. Revisit if a future npm/packaging version produces a real present-but-launchable-erroring stub, or on POSIX / an alternative package manager (bun) that yields one -- to close the last real-install gap on the CVE-2024-24576/R-11 security spine.

history.reason: SC-009 declares no blocking_assumptions; core rc!=0 feasibility pre-proven inline at /slice, rc==0 stub-mechanism routed to design-mode spike + exploratory charter

candidates.title: rebase-freshness-guard-before-validate
candidates.description: Add a rebase-freshness check that WARNS (not blocks) when a slice worktree's merge-base with the integration branch (aisdlc-uat) is behind the integration HEAD, run at /build-slice pre-finish and/or as a /validate-slice pre-gate. slice-009 branched from 8d17e90 before slice-008 merged (a358595) this session, so its stale-based worktree failed slice-008's shippability-anchored SHIP-008 regression (-m chained, exit 5) -- not a real coverage loss (R-14 corrected), but a stale-base artifact that cost a full /validate cycle + a manual rebase decision. A freshness warning would surface 'rebase onto aisdlc-uat before validating' proactively so a parallel/long-lived slice does not discover a sibling's just-merged regression the hard way. Loud + self-resolving on rebase; the guard just moves the discovery earlier and cheaper.
candidates.rationale: Retires the reframed R-14 process risk. Parallel slices are the norm in this project (slice-008 + slice-009 in flight together), so stale-base validate failures will recur; a cheap pre-validate/pre-finish freshness warning prevents wasted validate cycles without blocking legitimate work.

priority.blast_radius: pipeline tooling only (a pre-validate/pre-finish rebase-freshness warning); no production code

history.reason: no blocking assumptions; local git-plumbing tooling, no external-runtime feasibility risk
